claim: Let \(\mathcal L_{N,M}\) be the concrete quantum logic of a bipartite non-signalling box world with \(N\ge2\) binary-output inputs for Alice and \(M\ge2\) binary-output inputs for Bob, generated by the elementary events \([i,a;j,b]\). Every automorphism of the orthomodular poset \(\mathcal L_{N,M}\) is induced by permuting Alice's inputs, independently flipping the two outputs of each Alice input, permuting Bob's inputs, and independently flipping the two outputs of each Bob input; when \(N=M\), one may additionally interchange the two parties. Hence \[\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal L_{N,M})\cong (C_2\wr S_N)\times(C_2\wr S_M)\]for \(N\ne M\), while for \(N=M\) this product is extended by a \(C_2\) that swaps the two factors. In particular, \[|\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal L_{N,M})|=2^{N+M}N!M!\]when \(N\ne M\), and twice this number when \(N=M\). Thus the binary bipartite box logic has no hidden abstract symmetries beyond the standard operational relabelings.

integrity.computational_dependence: none for the proof; finite graph reconstruction checks are supplementary
integrity.novelty_scope: Exact exhaustion of all automorphisms of the binary bipartite box-world propositional logic by operational relabelings, including the party-swap exception and the group-order formula.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: The concrete logic, atom structure, and orthogonality rule are credited to Tylec--Kuś and Tylec--Kuś--Krajczok; standard Bell relabeling symmetries are credited to Bell-scenario symmetry literature.

scientific_limitations: The classification assumes two parties, at least two inputs per party, and exactly two outputs per input.
It concerns automorphisms of the full orthomodular propositional logic, not affine automorphisms of the non-signalling state polytope or stabilizers of individual Bell inequalities.
The one-input boundary cases are excluded because the atom orthogonality graph has extra degeneracies.
An equivalent no-hidden-symmetry statement may exist under exclusivity-graph or event-hypergraph terminology not surfaced by the searches.
title: All logical symmetries of a binary bipartite box world are operational relabelings
